{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Read the data
sales = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Verify that the only rows with commas are the QA orders
has_commas = sales['revenue'].str.contains(',', na=False)
qa_orders = sales.loc[has_commas]

# Confirm all QA orders have revenue '999,999.99'
assert (qa_orders['revenue'] == '999,999.99').all(), "Some QA orders have non-standard revenue"

# Now, check the distribution of customer_segment by channel
# This will show if the email channel is disproportionately composed of loyal customers
channel_segment = pd.crosstab(sales['channel'], sales['customer_segment'])
print("Cross-tabulation of channel vs customer_segment:")
print(channel_segment)

# Check the raw conversion rates by channel
raw_conversion = sales.groupby('channel')['converted'].mean()
print("\nRaw conversion rates by channel:")
print(raw_conversion)

# Now, compute conversion rates within each customer_segment
segment_conversion = sales.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['converted'].mean().unstack(level='customer_segment')
print("\nConversion rates by channel and segment:")
print(segment_conversion)

# Compute the difference in conversion rates within each segment
# We'll compute the difference: email - paid_search for each segment
# Then, compute a weighted average of these differences to estimate the campaign effect

# Get total counts per segment
segment_counts = sales.groupby('customer_segment').size()

# Compute the difference within each segment
diffs = segment_conversion['email'] - segment_conversion['paid_search']

# Weighted average of differences, using segment counts as weights
weighted_diff = (diffs * segment_counts).sum() / segment_counts.sum()

print(f"\nWeighted average difference in conversion rates (email - paid_search): {weighted_diff:.4f}")

# Also report the raw difference for comparison
raw_diff = raw_conversion['email'] - raw_conversion['paid_search']
print(f"Raw difference (email - paid_search): {raw_diff:.4f}")"}
